page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Below the text, one line of italic verse, set in the body with the signature "E" at the left foot and the catchword "Virgi-" at the right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: fus[?] aeris injurias umbonem quærere. Novi quidem vi-ros quosdam doctos reponere, quod pascua & subdi-ales pernoctationes quandoquidem in frigidioribus obti-neant oris, sicuti floridi interdum fiant Decembres, unde hoc multò magis in Palæstinâ fieri potuisse urgent, quippe sub clementiori Climate posita terra. Calorem conceptum testantur verba Kepleri, quando scribit.

„ Quod vero pascua nobis & subdiales pernoctationes ex evangelio objiciunt, quasi hæc hyemem non ad-mittant, ridiculum est: cum ne in Germania qui-dem desint interdum floridi Decembres, ut Itali-am, ut solis ardores Romæ mense Ianuario præter-eam. Imprimis vero in Palæstinâ major plerumque est serenitas Decembri, quam postea Februario & Martio. Aft, præter causam sibi ridendi argumen-tum spondet vir Doctus. Non est in quæstione, an non aliquando floridi Decembres, & bruma clementior sub climate Palæstinæ tolerabilem reddant aërem, ut vel subdiales pernoctationes ferre possint pastores? Verum dicimus ob brumæ incertitudinem non esse moris inter ejusdem climatis gentes, servos & pecora sua exponere vicissitudini temporis; cum omnis subita mutatio sit periculosa: inconstans est illa anni tempestas, & in omnes horas mutabilis, ut non soleant rustici peculium concredere serenitati brumæ fallaci. In ipsa Africa caulis inclusæ latent pecudes, quando circa solstitium versatur hybernum sol à nobis remotior. Saltem si Calphurnius ut putatur, suas ibi scripsit eclogas, quas Nemesiano Carthaginensi dicat; ille nobis testis erit, dum canit

p.i: Sed non ante greges in pascua mittite clausos Quam fuerit pacata Pales.

page.notes: Top-left word "fus" is cut off at the edge of the scan; the first letter is doubtful and may be a long s, so it is marked [?]. The reading of "horas" with a small mark after it, "fiant" versus "fiunt", and "Calphurnius" are copied as printed but are small and faint. The closing quotation mark of Kepler's passage is not visible; the opening marks „ at the start of lines are printed and are kept. The verse lines are italic and are treated as one stanza. The signature "E" sits at the lower left and the catchword "Virgi-" at the lower right.
